scenes.narration: Work on one habit at a time, not all thirteen at once.
Benjamin Franklin drew up a list of thirteen virtues he wanted to build. Chasing them all at once just scattered his attention.
So he gave each virtue a full week of focus, and let the others take their chances. Every evening, a small black dot for each slip, aiming to keep that week's line clean.
Thirteen weeks made a cycle, and he could run four cycles a year.
Like weeding a garden, he worked on one of the beds at a time, not all the bad herbs at once.

lines: Add the next when it's automatic.

scenes.narration: The same logic suits habit change today. Pick one behaviour, track it daily, and add the next only once the first feels automatic.
Choose one habit to focus on this week. Draw seven boxes on a card, and add a dot each evening you slip.
